23.1.6 Global Warming and Climate Change

Several climatic changes are attributed to the large emissions of pollutants into the atmosphere. Generally, the global climate changes are studied from two aspects.

i. Global warming caused by the greenhouse effect.

ii. Destruction of the ozone layer in the stratosphere. The later will be discussed in detail in “the chemistry of stratosphere”

Global warming

Global warming is the term used to described a gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth’s atmosphere and its oceans, a change that is believed to be permanent in the Earth’s climate.

The Earth maintains its long-term average temperature as a result of a balance between the heat received from the sun and the heat emitted to space by the Earth. These gases are called the greenhouse gases because they behave like glass cover of the green house which is responsible for maintaining the temperature of the greenhouse used to cultivate vegetation in cold climate regions.

The main greenhouse gases are CO₂, CH₄, SO₂, N₂O, O₃ and some other gases emitted from variety of industrial processes.

ځمکه خپله اوږدمهاله اوسطه تودوخه له لمر څخه د ترلاسه شوې تودوخې او د ځمکې له خوا فضا ته د خوشې شوې تودوخې ترمنځ د توازن په پایله کې ساتي. ځمکه له لمر څخه ډېری د لیدلو وړ وړانګې ترلاسه کوي او تودېږي. ځمکه خپله ډېری تودوخه د زیرسرو (IR) وړانګو په بڼه خوشې کوي (شکل 23.2). دا تودوخه په اتموسفیر کې ځینې شته ګازونه جذبوي او بېرته ځمکې ته د تودوخې په توګه لېږي. دا ګازونه تودوخه په اتموسفیر کې ساتي چې د ځمکې د تودوخې د زیاتېدو لامل کېږي او ”د شنه خونې اغېز“ بلل کېږي. دې ګازونو ته د شنه خونې ګازونه ځکه وايي چې د شنه خونې د ښیښه یي پوښ په څېر چلند کوي چې په سړو سیمو کې د سبزیو د کرلو لپاره د کارېدونکې شنه خونې تودوخه ساتي.

اصلي شنه خونې ګازونه CO₂، CH₄، SO₂، N₂O، O₃ او ځینې نور ګازونه دي چې له بېلابېلو صنعتي عملیو خوشې کېږي.

شکل 23.2 د شنه خونې اغېز انځور.

د شنه خونې په اغېز کې 50% ونډه لرونکی اصلي ګاز CO₂ دی. نور ګازونه (CH₄، CFCs، SO₂ او NOₓ) په ګډه پاتې 50% ونډه لري.

23.1.6 Global Warming and Climate Change

Several climatic changes are attributed to the large emissions of pollutants into the atmosphere. Generally, the global climate changes are studied from two aspects.

i. Global warming caused by the greenhouse effect.

ii. Destruction of the ozone layer in the stratosphere. The later will be discussed in detail in “the chemistry of stratosphere”

Global warming

Global warming is the term used to described a gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth’s atmosphere and its oceans, a change that is believed to be permanent in the Earth’s climate.

The Earth maintains its long-term average temperature as a result of a balance between the heat received from the sun and the heat emitted to space by the Earth. The Earth receives mostly visible radiations from the sun and gets heated. The Earth emits most of its heat in the form of infrared (IR) radiation (Figure 23.2). This heat is absorbed by some of the gases present in the atmosphere and redirect it back to the Earth as heat. These gases trap the heat into the atmosphere which results in increase in the Earth’s temperature and is called “the greenhouse effect”. These gases are called the greenhouse gases because they behave like glass cover of the green house which is responsible for maintaining the temperature of the greenhouse used to cultivate vegetation in cold climate regions.

The main greenhouse gases are CO₂, CH₄, SO₂, N₂O, O₃ and some other gases emitted from variety of industrial processes.

Figure 23.2 Illustration of greenhouse effect.

The major gas contributing 50% to greenhouse effect is CO₂. Other gases (CH₄, CFCs, SO₂ and NOₓ) together contribute the rest of 50%.

Human activities are increasing the atmospheric concentration of CO₂ and other greenhouse gases, thereby altering the way the sun’s heat is distributed on the Earth’s surface and in the atmosphere. In addition, the stratospheric ozone shield, which protects us from the sun’s UV radiations, is threatened by the emission of ozone-destroying chemicals. The Earth’s average temperature is being increased (global warming) which ultimately changes our climates. The most serious outcome would be rise in sea level, floods and pattern of rain fall.

23.1.7 Acid Rain

The concept of acid rain is also associated with polluted air. Acid rain, also called acid precipitation or acid deposition, precipitation possessing a pH of about 5.6 or below primarily produced from the emission of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogenous oxides (NOₓ; the combination of NO and NO₂) from human activities. Rain water is generally, slightly acidic (pH = 5.6) due to the dissolved CO₂ which is a common constituent (0.036%) of the Earth’s atmosphere making carbonic acid.
